rationale: B wins because it turns the weak spots into the story instead of politely parking them in the homework pile. Its markets angle, "Warby Parker got profitable — now it's spending on stores, and won't say what the exams earn," is the cleanest editor-ready tension in either set; A's comparable "Warby Parker is profitable and expanding" is true but flatter and leaves the undisclosed exam economics mostly in the proof list. A is good, but it carries one extra maybe-angle, "Warby Parker's retail expansion means a large new employer of optometrists," where "large" is doing work the facts have not earned.
gaps_in_A: "Warby Parker's retail expansion means a large new employer of optometrists" overstates the labor story; the update says most of 40 new stores will have optometrist-staffed exams, not how many hires or whether Warby employs them.
"Warby Parker was supposed to make optical stores obsolete" is a sharp contrarian line, but that founding-premise claim is not in the supplied facts; keep it only if sourced.
The investor angle underuses "exam-revenue contribution not broken out"; that disclosure gap is a real markets hook, not just an uncomfortable question.

Angle 5 leans into "healthcare access" before proving the pharmacy pilot includes anything beyond frames; the set admits it still needs to know "frames only, or frames plus a referral pathway for exams?"
gaps_in_B: "Warby Parker's next act is eye exams, not frames" is too absolute; the facts support exam expansion attached to stores, not a business pivot away from frames.
"the death of a retail thesis" is a little funeral-bell dramatic; the evidence supports DTC reversal, not a corpse.

"founding pitch was eliminating the middleman" and "pharmacy chains' fight to reinvent the front of store" may be true, but they are outside the supplied update and need sourcing before they become pitch copy.
It drops the optometry workforce/practice-management angle entirely; A showed there is a plausible trade-press lane if the employment model and staffing numbers can be nailed down.
